checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection
checked_sources.result: Fresh primary-source verification: non-partitioned e-detectors aggregate point-null e-processes over possible changepoints; aggregation weights determine ARL versus PFA control. This remains the global PFA/start-weight basis for the current detector design.

checked_sources.source: Kotłowski & Grünwald 2011, Maximum Likelihood vs. Sequential Normalized Maximum Likelihood in On-line Density Estimation
checked_sources.result: Fresh primary-source verification of sequential normalized maximum-likelihood framing and logarithmic-regret behavior for exponential families; role-local Gaussian conditional-SNML simulator remains consistent with the prior checkpointed formula.

checked_sources.source: Clopper & Pearson 1934, The Use of Confidence or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial
checked_sources.result: Fresh bibliographic verification of the exact binomial confidence-limit source used for one-sided Monte Carlo failure-probability bounds.

derived_results.claim: The H=48/T0=700 direct-joint I=1 scale is now randomized-continuum-certified over the entire two-dimensional Gaussian shell 1<=D_KL(Q||P)<=1.1, not merely the exact KL=1 contour or the pure variance-up ray.
derived_results.method: At each anchor and discrete offset, direct shared-path neighboring-pair failure is upper-bounded by one-sided Clopper-Pearson. Binary KL data processing converts that bound to a Gaussian target-to-anchor KL ball. The shell is partitioned in (mu,variance) rectangles; exact min/max D_KL(Q||P) conservatively identifies every rectangle that may intersect the shell. Because D_KL(Q||anchor) is jointly convex in (mu,variance), checking four corners certifies an entire rectangle. Stage2 anchor locations depend on stage1 uncovered cells but are evaluated with independent stage2 Monte Carlo randomness, avoiding data-dependent CP selection bias.
derived_results.scope: Discrete-time Gaussian step changes, conditional-SNML exact simulator, both mean signs by symmetry. Geometry is float64, not machine-interval verified. The result covers only KL in [1,1.1], not all KL>=1.

derived_results.claim: A dense independent engineering scan found no mixed mean/variance counterexample in the first shell; the largest observed joint failure remained on the I=1 boundary and failure decreased outward across the sampled I levels.
derived_results.scope: Engineering evidence only; it does not establish radial monotonicity. The randomized shell certificate above does not rely on this monotonicity observation.

derived_results.claim: When shell-cover holes determine new Monte Carlo anchor locations, reusing the same random paths for those data-dependent anchors would create an avoidable post-selection validity gap. Independent second-stage simulation restores conditional exact-binomial validity for the selected anchor set.
derived_results.consequence: Future adaptive randomized continuum covers should separate anchor discovery randomness from validation randomness, or predeclare the full candidate anchor family and union-bound it.

candidates_new.mechanism: Certify KL floors by successive finite radial shells using direct joint pair failure, independent validation for adaptively added anchors, binary-KL transport, and convex rectangular cell cover; hand off to an analytic high-information tail once one is proved.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the first shell's randomized/statistical construction; medium for scalability to the full unbounded KL floor until wider shells and an analytic tail are demonstrated.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Exact KL=1 plus a pure variance-up radial ray is enough to infer the full shell.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected as an inference. r76 explicitly covers mixed mean/variance directions in two dimensions rather than assuming radial monotonicity.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The first-stage fixed anchor grid alone closes the shell.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. On the 250x300 conservative rectangle grid, 1117 of 6353 potential shell cells were not fully covered after stage1. A second independent validation stage at 1073 deduplicated targeted anchors was needed.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Adaptive targeted anchors can be validated on the same Monte Carlo random paths that selected them without further accounting.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected as unsafe. r76 re-evaluated targeted anchors on independent stage2 randomness before making the simultaneous CP claim.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The 9-state bank is now adoption-grade for I_floor=1.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not yet. Only KL in [1,1.1] is closed. All stronger Gaussian alternatives KL>1.1 plus directed/interval numerical verification remain open.

frontier: Extend the H=48/T0=700 direct-joint cover outward from KL=1.1. Use the same fixed-first-stage plus independently validated targeted-second-stage protocol; adapt shell width based on observed anchor radii and cell-cover slack.
Seek an analytic high-information tail bound so finitely many radial shells can hand off above a finite KL radius rather than continuing randomized coverage indefinitely.

Replace float64 shell-intersection and target-to-anchor corner comparisons with directed-rounding or interval arithmetic; the current randomized confidence is explicit but geometric arithmetic is not machine-verified.

After all KL>=1 Gaussian directions are closed, repeat progressive radial shell certification for I_floor=0.5/H=96 and I_floor=0.25/H=192 before treating the 9-state {3,3,3} bank as a full-floor candidate.
After full-floor coverage, compare separable candidate-wise null-infimum with shared-null infimum-after-sum under the same 9-state schedule.
Do not generalize Gaussian evidence to heavy tails or non-Gaussian alternatives without a separately valid robust class.
exact_next_action: Run the next progressive shell for the H=48/T0=700 scale, beginning with 1.1<=D_KL(Q||P)<=1.3. Use a fixed contour/radial anchor grid for discovery, direct shared-path joint failure at all x=0..16, one-sided CP with explicit familywise budget, then add only uncovered-cell anchors and validate those locations on an independent random stream. If the shell closes with comfortable geometric slack, widen the next shell; if anchor count or weak margins explode, stop randomized expansion and derive an analytic tail lower bound from the exact Gaussian sufficient-statistic/SNML identity. In parallel implement interval/direct-rounding checks for the already closed [1,1.1] shell.
